source.title: The twin peaks of learning neural networks
source.authors: E. Demyanenko; Christoph Feinauer; E. M. Malatesta; Luca Saglietti

record.tranche_reason: The study reports width sweeps with test-error peaks near interpolation followed by declines at higher capacity, qualifying the claim that test error keeps falling past the width needed to fit the training data. It also relates a different sensitivity measure to generalization error.
record.gate_note: The paper varies architecture capacity and reports train error, test error, and Boolean mean dimension (BMD). Its optimizer and batch size are fixed; cited optimizer, dropout, and other studies are not its own results.
record.test_reason: The study reports training and test error across width sweeps in new architectures and settings, bearing on V2. A peak near interpolation followed by declining test error supports improvement beyond fitting; the peak alone does not qualify V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that BMD tracks increased input sensitivity and the generalization-error peak near interpolation across analytical and numerical settings, and relates to random sign-flip robustness. They do not establish that lower BMD universally implies better generalization: optimal regularization can leave a BMD peak despite monotonic test error, and excessive regularization can lower BMD while worsening generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Studies BMD and double-descent patterns using a random feature model, tanh MLPs, and ResNet-18 with Adam, batch size 128, learning rate 10−4, and optional L2 regularization or label noise. It does not reproduce the original random-label memorization or width-scaling experiments specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported patterns vary with label-noise level, L2 regularization, training-set size, architecture, and input distribution used to estimate mean dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: BMD peaks near the generalization-error peak across the tested width sweeps, but minimizing BMD alone does not ensure good generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BMD can indicate interpolation-related input sensitivity, but is not a universally monotonic predictor of test error.

fits_no_version.finding: Longer adversarial-initialization pretraining raises both subsequent test error and BMD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial initialization can jointly increase input sensitivity and test error in the tested MNIST MLP.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher BMD accompanies fewer random pixel sign flips needed to change a correct prediction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BMD negatively correlates with random sign-flip robustness in the tested MNIST MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing the distribution used to estimate mean dimension preserves the peak location in the tested MLP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of the mean-dimension peak is robust to the tested estimation distributions.

record.problems: Numerical findings are mainly presented in figures without exact values in the text. Several experiments average only 5 repetitions; the MNIST pixel-contribution heatmaps show one seed. The paper's BMD is a proxy measured on synthetic or resampled inputs, not the training distribution generally.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted; figure values are recorded as figure only because the supplied text does not provide recoverable numeric values.

untested.parts: Paired natural-label and fixed-random-label fits and held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.

The original one-hidden-layer ReLU recipe trained to convergence without explicit regularization, including downsampled CIFAR-10. Training duration and convergence checks for the numerical width sweeps are not supplied.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent generalization differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus matched random removals and retraining.

missing.what: Theoretical tanh random-feature width curves for a linear teacher, comparing MSE and cross-entropy losses across ridge strengths. These include higher-capacity generalization improvement and monotonic error under optimal regularization; the latter is selected by minimizing generalization error, not an independently validated tuning procedure.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's blanket limits_scope verdict. Interpolation-region double descent is compatible with V2's post-fitting improvement. BMD is an input-sensitivity measure, not V7's weight sharpness. Exact numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text; the verdicts rely on the authors' qualitative descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train the same architectures on fully random labels and natural labels to compare their held-out accuracy.

Does not use one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or the specified MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 setup; its MLP uses tanh, and other experiments use random feature models and ResNet-18. It does not isolate the width beyond the zero-training-error threshold as a monotonic test-error claim.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on the same image task or isolate local connectivity.
Uses Adam as a fixed optimizer; does not compare adaptive methods with SGD or vary optimizer tuning.
Batch size is fixed at 128; does not compare large and small batches or adapt training recipes.
Measures BMD, not magnitude-aware sharpness or weight perturbation tolerance, and does not compare it with norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples and retrain.

tranche.reason: Width sweeps test V2 in new settings using tanh random-feature models, a tanh MLP and ResNet-18. The interpolation-region peak does not itself qualify the subsequent width benefit.
